# Suggested Answers

## 1. Deterministic and stochastic processes

**(a)** Deterministic. Given the initial balance and the fixed interest rate, the account value is determined exactly at each time.

**(b)** Stochastic. The number of claims received during a year is uncertain and varies randomly.

**(c)** Stochastic. The temperature at noon varies from day to day and cannot be predicted with certainty.

## 2. Time-homogeneous and time-inhomogeneous Markov chains

A Markov chain is time-homogeneous if its transition probabilities do not depend on time. That is,

$$
p_{ij}^{(n)}=p_{ij}
$$

for all states $i,j$ and all time steps $n$.

For example, a driver's probability of moving between no-claims discount levels may depend on time if the insurer changes its discount rules over the years.

## 3. Periodicity and aperiodicity

The transition matrix is

$$
P=
\begin{pmatrix}
0 & 0 & 1\\
1 & 0 & 0\\
0 & 1 & 0
\end{pmatrix}.
$$

### (a) Determine the period of each state.

The chain moves deterministically through the cycle

$$
1\to 3\to 2\to 1.
$$

Starting from any state, the chain can return to that state only after $3,6,9,\ldots$ steps. Hence, the period of each state is

$$
d(i)=\gcd\{3,6,9,\ldots\}=3,
\qquad i=1,2,3.
$$

### (b) State whether the Markov chain is periodic or aperiodic.

All states have period $3$. Therefore, the Markov chain is **periodic**, with period $3$.

### (c) Does the chain have a stationary distribution? If so, find it.

Let $\boldsymbol{\pi}=(\pi_1,\pi_2,\pi_3)$ be a stationary distribution. It satisfies

$$
\boldsymbol{\pi}P=\boldsymbol{\pi},
\qquad
\pi_1+\pi_2+\pi_3=1.
$$

From $\boldsymbol{\pi}P=\boldsymbol{\pi}$, we obtain

$$
\pi_1=\pi_2,\qquad
\pi_2=\pi_3,\qquad
\pi_3=\pi_1.
$$

Thus, $\pi_1=\pi_2=\pi_3$. Using the normalisation condition,

$$
3\pi_1=1.
$$

Therefore, the stationary distribution is

$$
\boxed{\boldsymbol{\pi}=
\left(\frac13,\frac13,\frac13\right)}.
$$

### (d) Starting from state $1$, explain why the state probabilities do not converge to the stationary distribution.

Starting from state $1$, the chain moves through the states in the order

$$
1\to 3\to 2\to 1\to\cdots.
$$

Consequently, the distribution of $X_n$ cycles among the three point-mass distributions:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\Pr(X_n=\cdot\mid X_0=1)
&=(1,0,0), && n\equiv 0\pmod 3,\\
&=(0,0,1), && n\equiv 1\pmod 3,\\
&=(0,1,0), && n\equiv 2\pmod 3.
\end{aligned}
$$

These distributions oscillate and do not converge to $\boldsymbol{\pi}=(1/3,1/3,1/3)$. The chain has a stationary distribution, but its state probabilities do not converge to that distribution because the chain is periodic.
